To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

diamond nanoparticles treated by Fenton's reagent and hydrogen annealed at 500 ° C are able to support gold nanoparticles of small sizes and high activity for the photocatalytic degradation of phenol in water under natural sunlight irradiation.

hydrogen annealing of diamond-supported gold nanoparticles is an effective strategy for the preparation of efficient catalysts for sunlight-assisted degradation of organic contaminants by hydrogen peroxide.
the photocatalytic degradation of phenol by hydrogen peroxide in water is enhanced by using diamond-supported gold nanoparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new photocatalytic system for the degradation of organic pollutants in water, using diamond-supported gold catalyst and natural sunlight as the light source.

the development of a photocatalyst for the sunlight assisted peroxidation of a pollutant by H2O 2 in which the diamond support plays a dual role: (i) it provides a surface with high surface area for the deposition of gold nanoparticles, and (ii) it acts as an electron donor in the photocatalytic reaction.
the influence of hydrogen annealing of diamond nanoparticles on the photocatalysis activity of gold nanoparticles supported on diamond.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hydrogen annealing at 500 °Cs of diamond nanoparticles functionalized by the Fenton reaction leads to the formation of a diamond-supported gold catalyst with a higher catalytic activity in the natural sunlight-assistance phenol degradation by H2O 2 than those obtained by using the as-synthesized Fenton-treated diamond or those obtained after the hydrogen annealing of diamond at 700 °C.
diamond surface reduction by hydrogen treatment is a very efficient way to improve the photocatalytic performance of the diamond-supported gold catalyst.

hydrogen annealing at high temperature of diamond nanoparticles functionalized with Fenton-treated diamond is an efficient way to obtain a support for the deposition of gold nanoparticles with a high catalytic activity for the sunlight-assisted peroxide degradation of phenol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of carboxyl groups on the diamond surface is not required for the photocatalytic oxidation of phenol by hydrogen peroxide, although they are necessary for the adsorption of phenol on the diamond surface and for the formation of phenoxyl radicals.
the photocatalytic performance of the gold-diamond system is determined by a combination of the gold nanoparticle size, gold loading, and nature of the diamond surface.
hydrogen annealing of Fenton-treated diamond samples is an efficient way of modifying the surface properties of the diamond nanoparticles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photocatalytic performance can be improved by a careful choice of the diamond pretreatment and gold loading.
the hydrogen annealing of Fenton-treated diamond samples allows the preparation of highly efficient diamond supported gold catalysts.

the hydrogen treatment of Fenton-treated diamond samples is able to modify the nature of the surface functional groups and the gold nanoparticle size, leading to an enhancement of the photocatalytic performance of the diamond-supported gold catalyst for the degradation of organic pollutants in water.
